This is a long overdue review of this wonderful animal clinic - Middletown Animal Clinic!  True story.
At the beginning of the year, my sister went thru such distress with her beagle pup, Lady.  The pup was having dental issues and the former clinic my sister was taking Lady to (on Webster Ave near Fordham in the Bronx) handled this situation horribly.  That clinic is disorganized, lagged on returning patient calls, and money guzzlers!  I’ve seen my sister under a lot of pressure before but never to this extent.  When she shared her experience and told me Lady needs dental work because the pup had very bad gum disease, my sister was torn that no one was expressing concern over at the Webster Ave. vet clinic.  No one was returning her calls over a period of two months making Lady’s condition worst day by day.

I instantly made the call to Middletown Animal Clinic and it was the best decision we ever did! Middletown Animal Clinic jumped on this case immediately and took care of my sister and her pup with open arms! A true relief for my sister and Lady.  From the consultation appointment, the surgery and follow up post-op, Middletown Animal Clinic handled everything with care, compassion, diligence and above all - respect and love for the pup.  Lets not forget most importantly, Middletown Animal Clinic is mindful of the pawrents financials - they work with you to find the best resolution to achieve one goal - the best outcome for your fur baby.

Their staff is amazing!  From front of house, nurses, doctors and surgeons.  Now Lady is pain free living her best pup life - strong and healthy!  My sister officially switched Lady over to Middletown Animal Clinic and she will never look back nor consider another vet clinic.

Thank you Middletown Animal Clinic for everything!!!  🐶🫶🏼💛

I went to Middletown Animal Clinic under the impression that it was a reputable clinic. Unfortunately, I’ve had a horrible experience. There is a lack of communication and care at this vet.

I have a very special cat who is a cancer survivor. We recently noticed a mass growth on his left cheek. We immediately took him to the closest vet to get a check up. Unfortunately, he is traumatized and delicate so they were not able to examine him without sedation (which is understandable). When he was finally sedated, the clinic did blood work and x-rays. When we spoke to doctor Anastasiou we left the clinic feeling positive. He said my cat was healthy and all the results were perfectly normal. My cat was vomiting every day and I called the vet once again. He recommended Pepcid. We tried it and the cat was still showing signs of being ill. Still we trusted the word of the clinic. Despite countless follow ups for an estimate for a mass removal surgery, we never received.

Fast forward to today. The mass bursted out of his skin and he is bleeding all over my apartment. I once again called this vet and was told there were no doctors available so I am at a new clinic. The utter lack of care is quite clear.

While we were at this new vet, the doctor asked what was done for the mass itself. Was there a biopsy? Fluid removed and tested? These are the first things that should’ve been done is what we are being taught.

I called Middletown vet once again, to get a better understanding and a helpful technician helped me understand that ultimately all that was completed was a general exam, bloodwork and X-rays. Nothing for the mass itself. She was apologetic which I can appreciate but ultimately I feel this could’ve been avoided had Middletown Clinic taken their patient seriously and done a full work up instead of rushing to bill.

Due to my ignorance I trusted the word of the clinic but now I can’t help but blame myself for not seeking a second opinion.

I highly encourage folks to not visit this clinic. If I could give it 0 stars I would.
